# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old  <sub>[v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
- **Origin:** The States (Boston)  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has a remarkably beautiful, sensitive, and refined face with exquisite features, dark blue eyes, and chestnut curls that are later cropped short as he grows older. Though small for his age at ten, he grows very tall by sixteen. He resembles his father, Stephen Irving, and shares his dark blue eyes.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c19 P25](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0025), [v2 c19 P26](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0026), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c27 P23](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0023), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v2 c28 P9](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0009), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## Personality

Paul is a dreamy, imaginative, and meditative boy who possesses a rare, fine, and sweet soul akin to Anne Shirley's. He has a rich internal life filled with imaginary 'rock people' and poetic fancies about the world, though he is also polite, polite-mannered, and manly in games. He is deeply affectionate toward those he loves, especially his late mother and his father.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009), [v2 c19 P32](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0032), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033)_

- To honor and remember his deceased mother  <sub>[v2 c15 P2](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0002), [v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004), [v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>
- To grow up to be tall like his father  <sub>[v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)</sub>

## History

Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, at the shore road. Upon joining the Avonlea school, he quickly forms a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognizes his poetic genius and imaginative soul. Though well-liked by his classmates, he struggles secretly with his grandmother's strict diet of porridge and old-fashioned discipline. When Anne introduces him to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, Paul forms an instant affection for her. Later, Paul's father Stephen Irving unexpectedly visits Avonlea, reunites with Miss Lavendar, and marries her, giving Paul a second mother whom he fondly calls 'Mother Lavendar.' After the wedding, Paul moves to Boston with his father and stepmother, returning to Echo Lodge for summer vacations. As he grows older, he gradually leaves his childhood imaginary 'rock people' behind for games like football, while retaining his strong bond with Anne.

- Born to Stephen Irving and his first wife in Boston  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c15 P8](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0008), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I never got really acquainted with him until after my little mother died. But he’s splendid when you do get to know him. I love him the best in all the world, and Grandma Irving next, and then you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

> I think the new moon, teacher... is a little golden boat full of dreams.  <sub>[v2 c19 P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)</sub>

> Mrs. Lynde, father made a pretty good job of picking out my first mother and I could trust him to pick out just as good a one the second time.  <sub>[v2 c19 P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022)</sub>

> You see, that name belongs just to my own little mother, and I can’t give it to any one else. You know, teacher. But I call her ‘Mother Lavendar’ and I love her next best to father.  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>
